title: Barriers to entry
header_line: Jose's analysis of a book we are still naming. Not a summary of the book. Not affiliated with or endorsed by the author or publisher.

lines.text: What stops a competitor from copying you tomorrow?
Another thing that is really important, Jose said, is: what are the barriers to entry? Can competitors come in and lower my margin even more? Is there a price war? Can anybody get into the business?

That is what happened in the dot-com era, he said. People realized a web directory has no barrier to entry. Anybody can do a directory, and that is why it lost market share when a search engine came along with a massive barrier: its search algorithm.
Jose asked the students: what is the secret sauce of the solar division? A student said: the sales teams and the sales process. Jose said: that can be replicated. Anybody can build a sales team.

A student named a home battery pack. Jose said that is packaging: when you're not really inventing anything, you are creating an aesthetic and a package. A student said: you're rebranding something that already exists.

A student said: the brand awareness. Jose said: your branding is your protection. There is a thing called brand equity, the value your brand has. When people go to a supermarket they grab the soup they know, because of its history.

A student said it was the limitations of the kinds of roofs. Jose said: this is an opinion, and we will see over the history. I don't believe there is a barrier to entry. I believe he has to grab market share, build a brand, and go as fast as he can to become a household name.

The business is vulnerable because there isn't a secret sauce, he said. And a brand isn't necessarily protected: brands from other countries are flooding the market and taking share from established companies.
What is your barrier to entry, and is it real?

exercise.title: Five minutes
steps: Write what a competitor would need to copy you.
Write whether it takes one month or ten years.
Write your secret sauce, if you have one.
Write what your brand is worth to customers.
Write what you would do if a price war started.

check.q: What did Jose say anybody can build?
What did Jose say your branding is?
What did a student call a rebranded existing product?

recap: Know your barrier to entry. Build a brand that protects you.
